pbix.title: Download a report from the Power BI service to Power BI Desktop – Microsoft Learn
pbix.notes: PBIX is the file extension used for Power BI Desktop files. Microsoft Learn describes how a report or a semantic model can be pulled from the Power BI service into Power BI Desktop as a .pbix, which is the reverse of publishing from Desktop. A download can contain the report together with its data, a report with a live connection to the semantic model online (so the file holds no data), or an empty report that carries only the semantic model. At least the Contributor role in the workspace is required, and Power BI Desktop must be installed to open the file; using the current Desktop version is advised. Several cases cannot be downloaded, for example reports built on uploaded local Excel or CSV files, reports published before late 2016, and content deployed through deployment pipelines. Direct Lake models and models with incremental refresh can only be reached through a live connection, and semantic models with automatic aggregations cannot be exported as .pbix. Models above 50 GB are not supported for a data download. An administrator can switch the download feature off, in which case it does not appear in the service.

permission-creep-index.title: View data about the activity in your authorization system – Microsoft Entra Permissions Management
permission-creep-index.notes: The Permission Creep Index (PCI) is shown on the Microsoft Entra Permissions Management dashboard and is meant to make excess permissions visible across the monitored authorization systems. These systems are AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud Platform. The page does not give a formula or value ranges, but it describes high-risk as the number of users whose permissions go beyond what they normally or necessarily use. The dashboard groups identities into Low, Medium and High PCI categories, shows a bubble chart of high-risk identities, and lists the authorization systems with the largest recent change. A heatmap displays how many users contribute to a given score, and a trend view plus a downloadable PCI history report show how the index develops over time. Findings are split into identity findings, such as inactive or over-provisioned roles, and resource findings, such as unencrypted storage buckets or open security groups. Default service accounts and GCP-managed service accounts are not counted in the calculation. The documentation page is archived because the product was announced for retirement.

phi-3.title: Introducing Phi-3: Redefining what's possible with SLMs – Microsoft Azure Blog
phi-3.notes: Phi-3 is a family of small language models from Microsoft, offered to customers who build generative AI applications and want options at different points on the quality and cost scale. The first member, Phi-3-mini, is an instruction-tuned model with 3.8 billion parameters and context windows of 4K and 128K tokens; Phi-3-small and Phi-3-medium were announced as follow-ups for the Azure AI model catalog. The models are optimized for ONNX Runtime and Windows DirectML and are meant to run across GPUs, CPUs and mobile hardware, and Phi-3-mini is also offered as an NVIDIA NIM microservice. Phi-3-mini was made available through Azure AI Studio, Hugging Face and Ollama. Training relied on high-quality data in the spirit of the textbook-based approach, and safety work included reinforcement learning from human feedback, automated testing and manual red-teaming under Microsoft's Responsible AI Standard. Typical uses named are resource-constrained or offline scenarios, latency-sensitive tasks, simpler cost-sensitive workloads and easier fine-tuning. Because small models store less factual knowledge, results are weaker on fact-heavy benchmarks such as TriviaQA, and limits of use are documented in the model cards.

planning-optimization.title: Get started with master planning – Supply Chain Management (Planning Optimization)
planning-optimization.notes: Planning Optimization is the master planning engine of Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Master planning is delivered as an external service, the Planning Optimization add-in, which is installed per environment through Microsoft Dynamics Lifecycle Services and switched on with the Planning Optimization configuration key. Settings are found under Planning Optimization parameters in the master planning setup, where a connection status such as Connected shows whether the engine can be used. Prerequisites include a high-availability environment of tier 2 or higher (not OneBox), a recent enough Supply Chain Management version, Power Platform integration, and a Microsoft Entra account holding a Supply Chain Management license for the installation. The page states that no additional license or cost applies beyond existing Supply Chain Management licenses. The older master planning engine is deprecated but can run temporarily for individual companies, so migration can happen company by company. Limits include no support for on-premises deployments, availability only in listed Azure geographies, and batch jobs created for the old engine failing once Use Planning Optimization is set to Yes. Turning the engine off again is possible only in rare cases via Microsoft Support.

post-quantum-cryptography.title: Plan cryptographic agility and post-quantum readiness – Microsoft Learn
post-quantum-cryptography.notes: The page frames post-quantum cryptography as preparation for the possibility that future quantum computers could break some of the public-key algorithms that security controls depend on today. A named driver is the harvest now, decrypt later risk, where long-lived sensitive data is captured now and decrypted once the capability exists. Cryptography underpins authentication, digital signatures, software integrity and secure communication such as TLS, so the affected scope spans applications, identity systems, VPN and network gear, storage, IoT and operational technology, and partner integrations. The foundation it recommends is cryptographic agility, meaning the ability to change algorithms quickly and safely, together with an inventory of cryptographic use and trust chains, clear governance and a review of vendor timelines. The suggested approach runs through discovering vulnerable algorithm use, evaluating vendor support, planning phased migration waves with rollback options, and implementing with testing and evidence tracking. High-value assets, identity systems and long-lived data are prioritized. Migration is treated as a multi-year program, and some systems need new libraries, certificates, firmware or replacement hardware.

power-bi-report-builder.title: Power BI Report Builder – Microsoft Learn
power-bi-report-builder.notes: Power BI Report Builder is the authoring tool for paginated reports, which are print-friendly, multi-page, pixel-perfect reports that can show every row of a table. A report definition specifies which data is used, where it comes from and how the layout looks; the report can be previewed locally and then published to the Power BI service. Wizards help create tables, matrices, charts and maps, and free-form layouts suit documents such as invoices. Data can come from sources including SQL Server, Oracle, Power BI semantic models, Analysis Services, Azure SQL and OData, and reports support grouping, sorting, expressions, conditional formatting, parameters, drillthrough and document maps. Output can be exported to formats such as PDF, Excel, Word, CSV and XML, and subscriptions deliver published reports by e-mail. The download is free; with a free license publishing is limited to My Workspace, while Pro or Premium Per User allows other workspaces together with at least the Contributor role and build permission on the dataset. Existing reports from SQL Server Data Tools can be opened. Limits include that a parameter cannot be both multivalue and allow-null, and that running it as a virtualized application such as a Citrix published app is not supported.

private-5g.title: What is Azure Private 5G Core? – Microsoft Learn
private-5g.notes: Azure Private 5G Core is an Azure cloud service for deploying and managing 5G core network functions on an Azure Stack Edge device, forming part of an on-premises private mobile network for an enterprise. It connects to standards-compliant 4G and 5G standalone radio access networks and aims at low latency, secure connectivity for IoT devices and local data processing that does not depend on cloud connectivity. A packet core instance at each site includes functions such as AMF, SMF, UPF, PCF, AUSF, UDM and UDR, with an optional 4G mode for private LTE. Management happens centrally through the Azure portal and ARM APIs, SIMs and eSIMs are provisioned through SIM partners, and integration covers Azure Monitor, Resource Health, Event Hubs and Azure RBAC. A high-availability setup uses two devices. Radio equipment, SIMs, Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes and gateway routers are not part of the service and come from the customer or partners. Named uses include manufacturing analytics, warehouse automation, public safety, utilities and smart farming. The documentation page is archived: the service was announced for retirement, with migration to partner solutions recommended.

privileged-access-management.title: What Is Privileged Access Management (PAM)? – Microsoft Security
privileged-access-management.notes: Privileged access management is described as an identity security approach that watches for, detects and prevents unauthorized privileged access to critical resources. It combines people, processes and technology and is treated as a subset of identity and access management that controls and monitors what privileged users do after signing in. The stated aims are to limit how many users hold administrative capabilities, narrow the blast radius of an incident, reduce attack paths and support audits through activity logs. Typical capabilities include just-in-time and just-enough access, automated password management, multifactor authentication, secure remote access through gateways, recording of privileged sessions, analysis of unusual activity and account lifecycle automation. Implementation starts with full visibility of privileged accounts and application of least privilege, followed by controlling elevation, monitoring and auditing activity, and automating discovery and management. Privileged account types include domain administrators, service accounts, local and application administrator accounts and emergency accounts. Privileged Identity Management is contrasted as centering on time- and approval-based role activation. Technology alone is not considered enough.

product-dimensions.title: Product dimensions – Supply Chain Management (Dynamics 365)
product-dimensions.notes: In Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management there are five product dimensions: color, configuration, size, style and version. They are the characteristics that identify a product variant, are combined into dimension groups, and those groups are assigned to product masters. Values for size, color and style are created in the dimension and variant group setup, while configuration values usually come from the product configurator or the dimension-based configurator. Physical measurements are not product dimensions; they are set on the product master and apply to all variants. A product master needs at least one product dimension to generate variants, and on order lines the dimensions select the wanted variant. An example shows jeans offered in three colors and six sizes where only nine of the eighteen theoretical combinations actually exist as variants. The version dimension helps manufacturers track several product versions across the supply chain and is created as needed over the life cycle. Limits include no support for the version dimension in several areas such as vendor catalogs and in Commerce channels. Enabling it in production requires checking customizations that reference inventory dimensions, and it is on by default only for new systems from a certain release.

pstn.title: Plan your Teams PSTN connectivity – Microsoft Learn
pstn.notes: The page explains the public switched telephone network as the worldwide network of telephone lines, mobile networks and switching infrastructure that lets calls reach phone numbers anywhere. In Teams, PSTN connectivity lets users place and receive calls outside the organization, and voice apps such as auto attendants and call queues also need phone numbers. Calls between Teams users stay inside Teams and never touch the PSTN. Four connection options are described: a Microsoft Calling Plan where Microsoft is the carrier, Operator Connect with a certified third-party carrier, Teams Phone Mobile where a mobile operator number becomes the Teams number, and Direct Routing, which links any carrier through a certified session border controller. Options can be combined within one tenant. Users need a Teams Phone license plus a PSTN solution, which are separate things; the license grants calling features while the PSTN solution supplies numbers and access, including emergency calling. Teams Phone Mobile supports user numbers only. The page gives no prices, points to external directories for country availability, and mentions emergency support only for the United States.

publisher-verification.title: Publisher verification – Microsoft identity platform
publisher-verification.notes: Publisher verification gives users and administrators information about the authenticity of the organization that publishes an app integrated with the Microsoft identity platform. Microsoft confirms the publisher through a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account whose partner ID is linked to the app registration, and the app then shows a blue verified badge on the consent prompt and the enterprise applications page. Administrators can use verification status as a criterion in user consent policies. Requirements include that the partner account is the verified global account of the organization, the app is registered in a Microsoft Entra tenant with a work or school account rather than in Azure AD B2C, and the tenant is associated with that partner account. The publisher domain must match the e-mail domain used during verification and cannot be an onmicrosoft.com domain. The initiating user needs an application administrator role in Entra plus an admin role in Partner Center and must sign in with multifactor authentication. There is no fee and no license. It mainly applies to multitenant apps using OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect. The badge says nothing about app quality or certification, and national clouds are currently not supported.
